Katte Culture was recommended to me by a friend who had visited recently, and since we love exploring cafés across Bengaluru, it immediately made its way onto our list.

The café is tucked away in the quiet lanes of JP Nagar. It's a little far from where I stay, but the pleasant weather and surprisingly light Sunday traffic helped us get there in about 45 minutes. The moment we arrived, I liked the vibe. It felt like an old bungalow that had been thoughtfully converted into a café. There is a charming outdoor seating area surrounded by greenery, along with cosy indoor seating and a compact café space that houses the kitchen and counter.

What I appreciated right away was the simplicity of the menu. There aren't hundreds of options competing for your attention, which makes ordering a lot easier.

We started with the balsamic mushroom rosemary toast, and that was easily one of the highlights of the meal. It was packed with flavour, beautifully seasoned, and something I would happily order again. We also tried the cafreal chicken poi, which was equally enjoyable. The chicken ghee roast sandwich was another winner. Along with the food, we had coffee and finished with a slice of carrot cake. Honestly, everything we ordered was good.

What stood out most was the quality of the food. Every dish felt thoughtfully prepared, properly seasoned, and full of flavour. I had gone in with fairly high expectations because of all the recommendations, and I'm happy to say the food absolutely delivered. A perfect 10 on 10 for the food.

The service was prompt, the café was clean, and the atmosphere was exactly what I look for in a café. It was calm, quiet, and easy to have a conversation without competing with loud music. There was also a slight drizzle outside while we were there, which made the whole experience even more pleasant. If you're someone who likes working from cafés, this would be a great place to spend a few hours as well.

If I had to point out one area for improvement, it would be the pricing. The food is excellent, no doubt about that, but I felt the prices were slightly on the higher side. We spent close to ₹1,800–₹2,000 for what we ordered. While the quality justified part of the cost, I do think slightly more accessible pricing would make the experience even better.

Overall, Katte Culture is a café I genuinely enjoyed visiting. Great food, peaceful ambience, good service, and a setting that makes you want to slow down and enjoy the moment.

Will I visit again? Absolutely.

Iris Cafe and Kitchen at Jayanagar is a quaint and quiet cafe.   It has been designed to give it a heritage look with windows, doors and arches from the previous century.

The food was excellent, but the service left much to be desired.  Maybe they have a shortage of waiters.   After we were seated we had to wait for long and call one of them to get a menu.   It took another 10 minutes to ask for water to be served.   15 minutes after placing an order, we were told that Pina Colada was not available.    Another 20 minutes later they came back and said that one of the main courses - Ravioli that we ordered was not available.    In all it took over 45 minutes or more to get all the dishes that we subsequently ordered.

But whatever was served, was quite good and presented beautifully.

Crispy Lotus Stems Honey Chilli - These were good but too spicy for my liking.

Mushroom Chicken Steak - Grilled Chicken Breast with Mushroom Sauce, Veggies and Mashed Potatoes.    We loved this.   It was quite good and the quantity was substantial.

Paneer Fillet - Seared Paneer served with Pesto Sauce, Veggies and Herbed Rice.   This was also a tasty option for vegetarians.

Stuffed Mushrooms Au Gratin - Mushrooms stuffed, deep fried and Baked with Cheese on Top.  These were quite tasty too, but the need to deep fry could have been avoided.

Fruit Punch - This was a fruity ice cream shake with scoops of melon and quite refreshing.

They do have a lot of options and will definitely keep visiting.   Prices seem reasonable compared to a lot of new cafes in and around Jayanagar.

text.text:
A Perfect Afternoon Refuel at Sukino Cafe and Kitchen
When you find a spot where the aesthetic perfectly matches the quality of the menu, you know you’ve hit the jackpot. Sukino Cafe and Kitchen in Banashankari 2nd Stage is exactly that: a bright, minimalist sanctuary that feels worlds away from the bustling streets of Bangalore. My recent visit was a masterclass in how a cafe should operate: great food, an inviting atmosphere, and service that makes you feel like a regular from the moment you walk in.
Atmosphere & Vibe
Walking into Sukino, the first thing that strikes you is the clean, modern design. The space is flooded with soft light, featuring beautiful cane-backed chairs and sleek marble-topped tables. The wall boldly declares, "Today’s good mood is sponsored by coffee," and honestly, after one look at their professional espresso setup, I was inclined to believe them. It’s the kind of place that’s equally suited for a productive laptop session, a quiet reading hour, or a long-overdue catch-up with friends.
The Star of the Show: The Coffee
As a self-proclaimed coffee enthusiast, I have high standards, and the Sukino Style Cold Coffee didn’t just meet them; it blew them away. Served in a stunning double-walled glass that showed off a delicate swirl of chocolate syrup, it was topped with a generous peak of whipped cream and a fine dusting of cocoa.
The balance was outstanding. Often, cafes over-sweeten their cold brews to mask a mediocre bean, but here, the rich, bold notes of the coffee were the hero. The texture was velvety and indulgent without being cloying. Watching the cream blend into the dark espresso swirls was as satisfying as the first sip. If you are looking for a caffeine kick that feels like a treat, this is the drink to order.
Fresh Flavors: Nachos & Avocado Toast
To accompany the coffee, we started with the Loaded Nachos. You can tell immediately when a kitchen cares about freshness. The chips were perfectly crisp; no soggy edges here; and were piled high with a vibrant salsa, sliced black olives, and a dollop of cool sour cream. Every bite had that perfect crunch and a nice hit of acidity from the tomatoes.
The Avocado Toast was another highlight. Served on thick, toasted bread, the avocado mash was seasoned beautifully and topped with cherry tomatoes and olives. It’s a simple dish that many places get wrong, but Sukino keeps it fresh and flavorful, proving that high-quality ingredients speak for themselves.
The Service: A Shoutout to Beni
While the food and drink were top-tier, what truly elevated the experience was the service. Our waitress, Beni, was exceptional. She was attentive without being intrusive, ensuring our water was topped up and our dishes arrived exactly when we needed them. Her warm personality and professionalism added a layer of hospitality that you don’t always find in busy cafes. It’s clear that the staff here takes pride in their work, and Beni is a fantastic ambassador for the Sukino brand.
Final Verdict
Our total bill came to ₹1654.00, which, considering the quality of the meal and the beautiful environment, felt like excellent value. We also ordered the Pesto Pasta Veg and a Strawberry Mojito, and even opted for some takeaway to enjoy later.
Sukino Cafe and Kitchen has managed to create a space that feels both premium and cozy. Whether you’re coming for the outstanding coffee or the fresh, flavorful snacks, you’re bound to leave in a better mood than when you arrived.

Overall a disappointing experience. We felt that the staff are pretending to offer specialty coffee while serving up watered-down filter coffee from a press, and charging high prices for them. This is unprofessional and needs to be called out.

**Food: 3/5 | Service: 2/5**

Ordered the avocado toast, hazelnut iced coffee, chicken crepe, orange cinnamon brew, and chicken bagel.

The avocado toast is apparently their best seller, but the bread was way too hard — difficult to cut and even harder to bite into. The hazelnut iced coffee was decent, nothing special. The chicken crepe was actually good. The orange cinnamon brew was disappointing — tasted mostly of cinnamon with barely any coffee flavor and no sweetness. After asking them to add more coffee and some sugar syrup, it got better, but still not great. The chicken bagel was below average — very little chicken filling for what it costs.

The biggest issue here is the service. We sat at our table for 10 minutes and no one came to give us a menu. Had to ask for it ourselves. Then we asked a waiter for recommendations — he said he'd send someone else and just disappeared. Waited another 5 minutes. We kept having to turn around and wave at staff who were all just standing at the reception. No one actually walks around to check on tables.

At one point I noticed a table waiting for cutlery after their food had already been served. That says it all.

The prices feel high for what you get, both in terms of food quality and experience. If you're not in a rush and don't mind chasing the staff, it's manageable. But it really shouldn't be like that.

text.text:
MarcoPolo Café, Koramangala – Where Food Meets the Mic 🎤☕
If you love food and secretly believe you deserve a recording contract, then MarcoPolo Café in Koramangala is your place! This lively karaoke café is where people come to eat well, sing loudly, and forget they ever had stage fear.
🎤 The Vibe
MarcoPolo isn’t just a café — it’s a mini concert arena. The ambience is fun, energetic, and full of good vibes. You’ll see people cheering, clapping, and sometimes dramatically performing like they’re on a reality show finale. Whether you’re a bathroom singer or a hidden Arijit Singh, this place lets you unleash your talent without judgment.
🍜 Food Review (Because Singing Needs Fuel!)
Now let’s talk about the real co-stars — the food.
Mushroom Manchurian – Perfectly cooked, flavorful, and just the right amount of spice. A solid snack to munch on between songs.
Veg Soup – Warm, comforting, and light. Great to soothe your throat before hitting those high notes.
Chocolate Brownie with Nuts & Ice Cream – Absolute winner! Rich, gooey brownie topped with crunchy nuts and melting ice cream. Honestly, it deserved a standing ovation of its own.
The food here isn’t just an add-on — it’s genuinely very good and thoughtfully prepared.
👏 Service & Management
The service is very good, quick, and friendly. The staff keeps the energy going and ensures everyone is comfortable. A special mention to the manager, who is not only humble and approachable but also a surprisingly good singer! It’s always fun when the management joins the musical fun.
⭐ Final Verdict
MarcoPolo Café is a perfect combination of good food, great service, and pure entertainment. Whether you’re going with friends, planning a fun evening, or just want to sing your heart out, this place won’t disappoint.
Come for the food, stay for the karaoke, and leave feeling like a star. 🌟
Highly recommended for anyone who loves music, laughter, and lively vibes!

India Coffee House is truly one of Bengaluru’s most iconic and nostalgic cafés, and visiting it feels like stepping back into a simpler, old-world era. Earlier known for its presence around the heart of the city near MG Road, this place continues to carry that same legacy and charm even today at its Church Street location, just off Brigade Road.
The food is genuinely satisfying and full of comfort. Their South Indian breakfast options are delicious and feel authentic, and the café is also well known for its classic sandwiches, which are simple yet packed with flavour. If you enjoy egg-based items, their omelette and egg preparations are definitely worth trying as well. The menu may not feel “modern” or fancy, but that’s exactly the beauty of it — it delivers a taste that feels familiar, reliable, and timeless.

What makes India Coffee House stand out is not just the food, but the retro ambience and traditional service style. Even though Bengaluru has changed a lot over the years, this café has managed to retain its old-school look and feel, including the traditional uniform and attire of the servers, which adds to the authenticity of the experience. It has a unique character that you don’t find in most cafés today.
Another special part of the experience is the crowd — you can still see regular customers who seem deeply connected to the place, almost like it’s part of their routine and memories. That kind of loyalty and emotional attachment speaks volumes about what this café means to the city.

That said, with the changing times and increasing competition, some renovation and better maintenance (without disturbing the original look and identity) would definitely help this iconic café stay relevant for the long run. A little more visibility, better branding, and careful upgrades can help India Coffee House continue to thrive while keeping its heritage intact.

Overall, India Coffee House is a must-visit for anyone who loves Bengaluru’s old charm, authentic food, and a café experience that feels rich with history.

Yes, I am a beverage fan and without guilt! A foamy coffee with thick milk gives me a kick. At the same time, I love to be rooted to the culture that each place holds.

In this context, a few eateries in Bengaluru hold a significant heritage tag. One such place is the Indian Coffee House. The Indian Coffee House Co-Operative was established in August 19, 1957, with more than 400 cafés across the country. The outlets under the brand name Indian Coffee House were not just cafes for the earlier generations, but hubs for common people, students and intellectuals to socialize.

With competing cafés in many cities, only a handful of Indian Coffee Houses are left.

I have had pleasant experiences at multiple outlets of the cafe. I visited the Bengaluru outlet during the week of Kannada Rajyoutsav. We ordered coffee and cutlet. The beverage was light and the snacks were decent in taste. But one thing to notice was the attire of the waiters, which is common across Kolkata, Gwalior, and Bengaluru outlets - the ones that I have visited until now.

The Bengaluru Coffee House is housed at the Church Street junction behind Mahatma Gandhi (MG) Road.  Going by information available on the Internet, the original outlet was housed at the MG Road.

We had an amazing time at Cafe Azzure. The ambiance is awesome, and it easily offers the best view of the city and the metro rail, making the whole dining experience feel special.
​The food was the absolute highlight:
​French Fries (Peri Peri): Really good with a great kick!
​Thai Basil Pesto: The flavoring in the pesto paste was AWESOME.
​Truffle Oil Mushroom Pizza: Really amazing, perfectly baked, and packed with flavor.
​Enchanted By The Sakura Mist: A beautiful and unique drink. It was really nice, and I’ve honestly never had anything like it anywhere else.
​We also tried the Broccoli Cheddar Soup and the Bombay Masala Sandwich, and everything tasted fresh and delicious. Definitely worth every single penny. Highly recommended for great food, stunning views, and excellent value for money!
